12-year-old boy brought in by mother with a 6-day history of productive cough with yellow sputum, fevers at home, and breathlessness. Associated symptoms: chills and sweats, generalised myalgia, and poor feeding.

Background: Mild asthma on salbutamol PRN; otherwise well, immunisations up to date.

O/E: T 39.0 degC, HR 76 bpm, RR 28/min, BP 105/65 mmHg, SpO2 97% on room air. Reduced chest expansion and dullness at the both bases with audible crackles.

CXR: patchy bilateral consolidation. Bloods: WCC 13.7, CRP 169 mg/L, urea 9.7 mmol/L; blood cultures sent.

Assessment: community-acquired pneumonia (patchy bilateral consolidation) - severe severity.

Plan: Transferred to PICU: high-flow nasal cannula oxygen, IV co-amoxiclav, continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring.
